previous_science_card.assessment: The source packet provides a complete experimental and theoretical description of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) realized via single-photon quantum walks. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta of the PUAMO, given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent. The source reports the full parameter-space phase scans for the Hermitian (eta=0) and non-Hermitian (eta=0.1) cases, and the Lyapunov formula is explicitly given in the supplementary material. The extraction captures the central quantitative relation with all structural constants as named, anchored parameters. The source contains an internal inconsistency in the PT-threshold wording (main text states eta_PT = -log(lambda_0) while the supplementary and reported numeric value 0.119 for lambda_1=0.25, lambda_2=0.5 imply eta_PT = log(lambda_0)/(2*pi)), but this does not affect the selected Lyapunov equations, which are internally consistent. Therefore case_authoring_ready is set to true.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper reports the first experimental realization of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) using single-photon quantum walks. It observes metal-insulator transitions in the Hermitian limit, PT-symmetry-breaking transitions, and a novel spectral transition where all quasienergies become purely imaginary. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta, which quantifies the inverse localization length and is given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent.
